samples.label: Careful paper (sample)
samples.title: Sample: Measuring self-improvement in coding agents on held-out tasks (test data)
samples.authors: Sample Author A, Sample Author B (test data)
samples.text: Abstract. We study whether a coding agent that edits its own scaffolding improves over successive rounds, a small step toward recursive self-improvement. We evaluated 3 agent variants on 500 tasks drawn from a held-out test set that none of the variants saw during development. Compared with the unmodified baseline, the self-edited agent solved 41.2% of tasks versus 35.0%, a gain of 6.2 points (95% confidence interval 3.9 to 8.5, across 5 seeds). Most of the gain came from better test selection; an ablation that removes it keeps only 1.1 points. Limitations: the tasks are short, gains shrink after the third round, and we do not claim the effect generalizes to longer projects. Code and data are available at github.com/sample-org/sample-repo.

samples.title: Sample: comment on an interpretability result (test data)
samples.text: Interesting result on sparse autoencoder features, but the steering effect was only shown on 20 prompts and there is no baseline with a random direction. I would want held-out prompts before reading much into it.
